lines: Haitian conflict 2026 Croix-des-Bouquets gang ambush Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele announces the start of a military operation to rescue four Air Force technicians. The technicians, attached to the international Gang Suppression Force, were taken hostage after gangs attacked their armored vehicle on 18 October. (Reuters)

2026 Iran war fuel crisis South Africa cuts fuel levies by R3.00 (US$0.18) per litre of diesel and R1.50 ($0.09) per litre of petrol from November 4 to December 1 after fuel prices reach record highs. (AFP)

The North Sea Transition Authority (NSTA) of the United Kingdom approves production from the Jackdaw gas field after energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh authorized the NSTA to grant consent, allowing operator Adura to begin supplying gas by late October. (UPI)

Houthi–Saudi conflict, Saudi Arabia–United States relations The U.S. Department of State orders non-emergency employees at its embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, to leave the country as Houthi attacks ramp up. (Al Jazeera)

Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war United States special envoy Steve Witkoff arrives in Saint Petersburg to talk with Russian president Vladimir Putin about potentially resolving the war with Ukraine. Putin states he would resume U.S.-mediated trilateral peace talks with Ukraine and the United States, on or after November 10. (Reuters) (Reuters)

American military veteran Stephen James Hubbard, who was arrested by Russian authorities in 2022 during the Battle of Izium, is released from custody during the meeting between Putin and Witkoff. (AP) (BBC News)

Qatar, Turkey, Pakistan, and Indonesia jointly sign the Badr Memorandum of Understanding, a major agreement to deepen their defence industry cooperation. The agreement aims to support joint military production projects and strengthen cooperation in technical training, research, and development. (Reuters) (Al Jazeera) (Dawn)

Lawsuits involving Meta Platforms A district judge in New Mexico, United States, orders Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found it guilty of misleading Facebook users about privacy violations, marking its largest fine ever. (Al Jazeera)

Mexican war on drugs, Mexico–United States relations The Mexican government launches an investigation into former attorney general of Chihuahua César Jáuregui Robles for allowing U.S. Central Intelligence Agency agents to take part in an anti-drug trafficking operation in Chihuahua earlier this year. Under Mexican law, the federal government must approve the activities of foreign forces on Mexican soil. (Al Jazeera)

2026 Quebec general election, Plamondon ministry Paul St-Pierre Plamondon is sworn in as the 34th premier of Quebec following the Parti Québécois's victory in the general election. (The Globe and Mail)

2022–2026 video game industry layoffs American video game publisher Electronic Arts, which was recently bought-out by the Saudi Public Investment Fund, announces the closing of its Canadian studio BioWare. (Kotaku)
